title: Judge Says California Must Keep Counting Ballots as They Are
summary: A federal judge in Los Angeles has said California must keep handling ballots the way it already does. On Wednesday, Judge David O. Carter turned down a request from the Trump administration. The administration wanted the state to stop processing ballots from up to 20,000 people it said were likely noncitizens. More than 3.7 million people had already voted in California. The state mails ballots to all 23 million registered voters. More than 500,000 ballots had already been processed. Once a ballot is taken out of its envelope, county officials said, it can no longer be matched to its voter. Carter wrote that separating the ballots now would cause chaos and disrupt an election already underway. He said it could take away votes from United States citizens. The administration had sued in mid-October. It said California missed a 48-hour deadline to check a list of 20,000 people. Justice Department lawyers said they would appeal right away. Bill Essayli, a First Assistant U.S. Attorney, said separating a ballot would not stop it from being counted later.
why_it_matters: Rules about counting votes matter to your family because they help make sure every citizen's vote counts fairly in an election.
